question: A node is scored to a tier that names no host in the config. What runs it?

options.label: `dispatch.host` runs it, exactly as before this feature
options.reason: A project with only `dispatch.host` set keeps working untouched, and one tier can be moved to another host without filling the other two. It is what `parseConfig` already does for every other missing key.
options.costLater: A typo in a tier key sends the work to the default host at the default model, and nobody notices unless the run record says the fallback was used — so the record has to say it, and `sober status` has to show it.

options.label: Not started — the refusal names the node, the tier and the key to set
options.reason: ADR 0048's rule: refused, not defaulted. The user reads one sentence before any worktree exists instead of a wrong invoice three minutes later.
options.costLater: Every project that adopts tiers has to fill all three before any scored node starts, and `dispatch.host` goes dead the moment `dispatch.tiers` exists — two settings that mean the same thing, one of them ignored.

options.label: The schema requires all three tiers once `dispatch.tiers` is present; a partial table is a broken config
options.reason: The error arrives at config read, before any node is scored — the same place a wrong `timeoutMinutes` is caught today.
options.costLater: A config being edited by hand breaks `sober status` until the third line is written, and `sober init` has to emit the whole table or none of it.
